HIVE — MAIN CHARACTER RIG (from your in-progress placement)

Built from the layout you exported from the editor and dropped in Downloads. Heads up: your export only had 11 of the 16 pieces (torso, pelvis, both upper_arm/forearm, both shin/foot, and head) — neck, both thighs, and both hands weren't in it, so those five are filled in from my auto-seed positions, not your placement. Your forearm rotation (-22° far / -15° near) is preserved here as a static bend baked into the art, with the walk-cycle elbow motion animating on top of it.

What this is: the 10 named parts from the new compact-style reference sheet (one of each — no left/right, true side view), duplicated into a "near" and "far" copy for each limb (near drawn in front of the torso, far drawn behind it, same trick every 2D side-view game uses for depth), auto-stacked into a standing paperdoll with no manual placement. Why this sheet exists: the previous side-view sheet's thigh/forearm came out roughly 4:1 height-to-width, which fought the auto-placement heuristics no matter how the joint overlap was tuned and made hand-assembly in the editor feel like nothing would sit right. This sheet was generated with an explicit compact-proportions/simplified-detail prompt instead (closer to typical 2D game sprite ratios), and the auto pose above is assembled straight from it with no manual correction — it's the new baseline to hand-place from in the editor, not a stopgap.

v4 knee/elbow fix: the earlier "delayed drag" knee motion was too subtle to read on limbs this long — it never looked like an actual bend. Replaced it with a stance/swing-gated fold: zero knee rotation through the whole stance half of the cycle (leg planted, straight, bearing weight) and a single pronounced fold peaking at mid-swing (foot lifted, clearing the ground) — matching where real knee flexion actually peaks, instead of a uniform pendulum with no distinction between "planted" and "recovering." Same gating on the elbows. Pelvis roll (hips tilt toward whichever leg is planted), opposite-phase torso counter-twist (contrapposto), arm-opposite-leg swing, and the body bob peaking at each leg's passing pose are all still in from v2/v3.
